runtime: Windows 11 Enterprise 24H2 ja-JP (build 26100), Windows PowerShell 5.1, domain-joined VM in an isolated lab forest, run elevated as a domain administrator.
procedure: Dot-sourced the script. Used it to add test domain credentials to the SYSTEM vault for each target form with a low-privileged user, ran the listing, ran an LDAP write as SYSTEM against the computer's own object through the DC FQDN, inspected klist -li 0x3e7, then removed each entry with Remove-SystemSavedCredential. Also embedded the functions in a UTF-8 .bat/PowerShell polyglot and ran it with no credential, with a DC credential plus operator refusal, with DELETE, and with the network adapter disabled.
expected: Default entries are not flagged. DC-targeted domain credentials are flagged and make the SYSTEM write fail as the saved user. Deletion restores the computer identity. An unreachable DC fails closed. Temporary tasks and files are removed.
observed: Baseline write succeeded with the computer account as LDAP client. Short DC name, DC FQDN, *.domain and *.parent-domain targets were flagged, the write was denied and the LDAP ticket client became the saved user. Domain DNS name, NetBIOS name and DC IP were flagged but did not affect a bind to the DC FQDN. Other-server and generic targets were not flagged and had no effect. The default WindowsLive entry was not flagged. Without a DC, the check threw. Refusal and lowercase input deleted nothing. DELETE removed only the DC-targeted entry. No temporary task or output file remained.
limitations: dsregcmd /join was not run; the write test used telephoneNumber from the same Personal Information property set instead of userCertificate.
Not exercised: battery operation, non-Japanese Windows, and the * and DOMAIN\* targets, which cmdkey /add rejected.
The polyglot flow is an example around these functions and is not a catalog artifact.
